title: Happier at Home: Kiss More, Jump More, Abandon a Project, Read Samuel Johnson, and My Other Experiments in the Practice of Everyday Life
author: Gretchen Rubin
target_audience: Adults seeking greater happiness and satisfaction at home
Individuals interested in personal growth and wellness
Fans of Gretchen Rubin’s previous work (especially 'The Happiness Project')
Readers interested in practical strategies for improving everyday life
People looking to cultivate positive family and home environments
core_themes: Intentional living and the pursuit of happiness
The importance of small changes in cultivating contentment
Mindfulness and presence in family and home life
Building stronger connections with loved ones
Appreciating ordinary moments and domestic routines
primary_purpose: To chronicle the author’s year-long journey of making her home a happier place, offering practical ideas and personal insights for readers to try their own experiments for increasing happiness and satisfaction within their home and family life.

structure_format.narrative_style: First-person, reflective, narrative-driven with a mix of memoir and how-to advice
structure_format.organization: Organized by months, each focusing on a specific theme or area of home life; includes experiments, resolutions, and monthly reflections
features: References to literature, philosophy, and research on happiness

key_concepts_lessons: Small, intentional changes can create a more joyful home environment.
Self-knowledge and personal values are essential for choosing meaningful happiness strategies.
Focusing on relationships and meaningful connections boosts overall well-being.
Physical surroundings impact emotional states and productivity.
Letting go of projects or obligations that no longer serve purpose can lead to greater contentment.
Cultivating rituals, traditions, and appreciation for the everyday deepens one’s sense of belonging.
Happiness is a process that involves continual reflection and experimentation.
notable_features: Month-by-month happiness experiments tailored to home life
Blend of practical advice, memoir, and research-based insights
Focus on both internal (mindset) and external (environmental) factors
Relatable everyday scenarios drawn from the author’s own family
Follow-up to the bestselling 'The Happiness Project'
cultural_historical_context: Published in the wake of increasing interest in positive psychology and the science of happiness, the book responds to growing cultural emphasis on work/life balance and the importance of home as a source of fulfillment. Rubin’s work reflects early 2010s trends in memoir-driven self-help literature and the popularity of personal improvement projects.
reception_impact: Well-received by readers of self-help and personal development genres, especially fans of Rubin’s previous work
Praised for its relatable, warm, and practical approach
Critics note the book’s emphasis on small-scale, individual action rather than systemic change
Inspired readers to undertake their own happiness projects at home
comparable_titles: The Happiness Project by Gretchen Rubin
The Art of Happiness by Dalai Lama and Howard Cutler
Simple Abundance by Sarah Ban Breathnach
The Gifts of Imperfection by Brené Brown
